text:
elaine: Quick sync — we need final answers for Q2 model-catalog scope. Three decision points: (1) onboarding bench pass criteria, (2) pin TTL + extension policy for enterprise, (3) migration incentives/credits. Meeting in 45m if folks can join.

mohit: can we reduce options for pin TTL? ops + sales need a single recommendation. i vote 60d default + paid 90/180 extensions.

jackie: 60d is okay for small tenants but BigCorp will push for 180. propose we do 60d default + 90d grace for enterprise auto-extend with contract flag.

anne: agree on 60d default. also recommend an "opt-in longpin" checkbox for enterprise trials to avoid emergency migrations.

elaine: good. on onboarding bench: we need both perf and quality thresholds. suggested draft: P95 latency <=150ms, throughput >=8 req/s per GPU for gen workloads, embedding recall F1 >=0.88 on our eval set.

simon: latency target looks tight for long-context models. can we make perf conditions conditional on quantization: if quantized variant used, allow P95 <=200ms. quality thresholds must be strict though (F1 >=0.88).

mohit: +1 to conditional perf. also add a failure mode: if model fails perf but passes quality, allow a "compat-shim" pin with reduced default qps and explicit warning in catalog.

jackie: we should also surface an "operational impact" score in catalog entry (est. tokens/sec cost delta, retry rate risk). helps sales negotiate migration credits.

neil-bot: deploy-bot: canary slots available in us-west-2: 3/5. Use `/canary create --slot=auto --region=us-west-2` to reserve. :robot_face:

elaine: good call on canaries. rollout plan: canary cohort (5 customers) 48h, expand to 20 customers 7d, GA after 14d with health gates. Health gates = error rate <0.5%, perf within agreed band, no quality regressions on 3 smoke prompts.

anne: on migration incentives: propose credits = 10% of first 3 months' estimated usage + 2 weeks concierge migration support for enterprise. smaller tenants get 1 month credit or free pin extension.

mohit: add automatic fallback policy: if new model degrades in production, traffic must auto-failover to previous pinned version for affected tenants until a patch or rollback completes. add SLA language.

jackie: question: do we allow quantized variants to be pinned separately from full-precision models (i.e., separate catalog entries)? Ops prefers pin to model-id so runtime can pick best flavor.

simon: prefer model-id pin with runtime flavor selection + explicit bench metadata per flavor. avoids duplicate catalog noise.

elaine: consensus summary to take to leadership:
- Pin TTL: 60d default, 90/180 enterprise extensions via contract or paid opt-in.
- Bench pass: quality (embedding F1 >=0.88) + perf conditional on flavor (P95 <=150ms FP, <=200ms quant).
- Rollout: 48h canary -> 7d broaden -> 14d GA with health gates (error <0.5%, no regressions).
- Migration incentives: 10% credits + 2w concierge (enterprise), 1mo credit/small tenants.
- Operational: compat-shim allowed with reduced qps + explicit catalog warning; auto-fallback to previous pinned version on regressions.

elaine: I’ll put this in a follow-up doc and tag the execs. if anyone has objections, reply here before I send. :raised_hands:

jackie: no objections from me. please include the opt-in longpin UX copy so support can triage.

mohit: ok from infra. will validate canary automation pre-meeting.

neil-bot: infra-check: canary automation tests: PASS on staging, 2/3 required hooks present.

elaine: thanks all — will create PR with the spec + demo bench configs.

mohit: handy snippet for bench config if you want to include in PR:

```
bench_config:
  latency_p95_ms: 150
  embedding_f1_min: 0.88
  throughput_min: 8
  flavor_exceptions:
    quantized:
      latency_p95_ms: 200
```

jackie: awesome, thanks.

elaine: tagging @product-leads and @sales-ops in the PR once it's up.
